newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH VATT JOBS STUDY MAY BE OUTDATED - ECONOMISTS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH VATT JOBS STUDY MAY BE OUTDATED - ECONOMISTS.

text.p: The findings of a study released on Tuesday on the eagerness of the unemployed to seek work rather than living off unemployment benefits may not accurately reflect today's situation, economists said.
The study by the Government Economic Research Institute (VATT) focused on the economic incentives of taking a job compared to staying unemployed.

The study covered people out of work in 1990-92 when earnings-related jobless benefits were high after an econmic boom in the late 1980s, and before public sector spending cuts set in as the recession of the early 1990s deepened.

"At that time the level of unemployment benefits was very high," OKOBANK chief economist Matti Huomo told Reuters by telephone. "One can doubt whether today's world and the world in those days are that similar," he added.
"It is certainly too distant from today," he said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
